claims.explanation: Nocodazole kills cells by disrupting microtubule polymerization, which preferentially triggers mitotic arrest and apoptosis in cells that rapidly transit the cell cycle and have intact spindle assembly checkpoint signaling. Selectively killed lines are enriched for TP53 mutation and for mutations that drive proliferation (KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, PTEN loss), whereas protected lines include several with BRAF mutation without TP53 loss and lines with mutations that may impair mitotic checkpoint/apoptotic coupling. The pattern suggests that sensitivity is determined by high mitotic rate combined with defective p53-dependent arrest, rather than by a single lineage.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is highly enriched in killed lines and loss of p53-mediated arrest promotes mitotic catastrophe after spindle disruption
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among killed lines, consistent with increased proliferative drive and mitotic dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma and other lines appear in the killed set, suggesting MAPK-driven proliferation increases reliance on microtubule dynamics
PTEN loss co-occurs with killed lines and may enhance PI3K-driven proliferation and mitotic entry
PIK3CA mutation is present in several killed lines and may promote proliferation and survival signaling that increases mitotic vulnerability
SMARCA4 mutation appears in multiple killed lines and may impair chromatin-based stress responses, increasing sensitivity to mitotic poisons
STK11 mutation is seen in killed lung lines and may alter metabolic/checkpoint responses to microtubule disruption
CDKN2A loss is common in killed lines and removes a cell-cycle brake, favoring mitotic entry and nocodazole sensitivity
ARID1A mutation is enriched in killed lines and may compromise chromatin remodeling needed for cell-cycle arrest
FBXW7 mutation appears in several killed lines and may stabilize mitotic regulators, increasing dependence on spindle integrity
NF1 mutation in killed lines may increase RAS pathway activity and proliferation, sensitizing to microtubule inhibition
Higher tubulin expression could buffer nocodazole effects by increasing polymer mass, though direct evidence is not in the provided abstracts
